candidate.answerReason: With x>3, the equal-time equation gives x=21. The downstream and upstream speeds are 24 and 18 kilometers per hour, giving two hours for each trip.

methods.label: Equate downstream and upstream times
methods.explanation: Set up the equation \(\frac{48}{x+3}=\frac{36}{x-3}\). Clearing the denominators gives \(48(x-3)=36(x+3)\), so \(x=21\). Checking confirms that it fits the practical situation.
methods.levelReason: Uses Grade 8 rational equations and Grade 7 linear-equation solving.

methods.label: Use the speed and distance differences
methods.explanation: The downstream and upstream speeds are \(x+3\) and \(x-3\), with \(x>3\) for upstream travel. Their difference is \(3+3=6\) kilometers per hour. Over equal durations, this produces the distance difference \(48-36=12\) kilometers, so the common duration is \(12\div6=2\) hours. The downstream speed is therefore \(48\div2=24\) kilometers per hour, giving \(x=24-3=21\) kilometers per hour. The upstream speed is then \(18>0\), and \(36\div18=2\) hours as required.
methods.levelReason: Uses elementary arithmetic to find the common duration before recovering the still-water speed.

candidate.annotationRationale: The target is determining still-water speed from equal travel times. Both methods use distance = speed × time. Clearing variable denominators and solving the resulting linear equation are local to the first route; recovering duration from the distance and speed differences is local to the second. candidate.changeReason: The downstream and upstream denominators correctly include opposite current effects. The resulting x=21 exceeds the current speed and gives equal two-hour durations, so the current explanation is sufficient.
